subject: Urban Planning
title: Buried Utilities: The Case for Undergrounding
description: A fast breakdown of Buried Utilities: The Case for Undergrounding for builders.

hook.text: Tokyo has no overhead power lines. European cities buried theirs decades ago. America still has wooden poles from the 1950s.

buildup.text: Overhead power lines cause most weather-related blackouts. Fallen trees and ice storms take out power for millions annually.

discovery.text: Underground cables are 10 times more expensive to install but last 3 times longer and resist storms completely.

twist.text: After Hurricane Maria destroyed Puerto Rico's grid, rebuilding above ground was cheaper. Poverty forced the same design.

climax.text: San Diego is burying power lines in fire-prone areas after utility equipment sparked devastating wildfires.

punchline.text: Bury the wires. Pay more now. Or pay for every storm forever.

quiz.question: Why do most American cities still use overhead power lines?
options: Underground cables don't work in American soil conditions
Burying cables costs 10 times more than overhead installation
Federal regulations prohibit underground utilities in most zones
